segments.text: Spot tokens show their PnL against the live price. If you bought them at a fixed price and the price hasn't moved, your PnL is zero.

Freeze on: The creator can freeze your tokens. Mint on: The creator can make more tokens, so supply is not fixed. Low liquidity: Thin trading, so you can get a bad price in. New: A new token with no track record yet.

PnL only shows for tokens you bought and sold, not just hold. If you only hold a token without selling it, there's no PnL yet. You can check your spot positions in Earn > Positions to see if you have any open trades with PnL.
Mint is the ability to create more tokens, so a mint-on token can be pumped. Freeze means the creator can freeze your tokens, so a freeze-on token can be locked out.
No. Refusals only block buys, not sells. You can still sell tokens you hold, and the app will show a review for each sale.

A big price impact means the sale cost you more than it should have, because selling a large piece of a thin pool moved the price against you. It's worse on small pools and when you hold a lot of one token. You can reduce it by selling smaller at a time, or by buying back part of what you sold to rebalance.

The token list comes from Solana's official RPC, so it's the same list that runs the Solana blockchain. The verified flag means Jupiter has checked the token and its liquidity is above a minimum. It does not mean the token is safe from scams or rug pulls.
Unverified means the token hasn't been checked by Jupiter, so it may be a scam. Only buy tokens that are verified by Jupiter.

Spot tokens are Solana tokens you hold in your wallet, like USDC or a token from a swap. They sit in your wallet and can be sent, sold or deposited into Aave. Spot tokens don't earn interest by themselves.

No, the buy refusal doesn't apply to selling. You can still sell a token you hold, but only if it's one you already own and the market has liquidity for it. The app won't let you sell something you don't have. If you want to sell a token you don't currently hold, you'd need to first swap it into your wallet.
Sure. What's the token's ticker or mint address?

Unverified means the token isn't checked by Jupiter. Freeze on means its creator can freeze your tokens, so you can lose them. Mint on means the creator can make more tokens, so it can be inflationary. Low liquidity means a price swing when you buy or sell. New means it's new, so it may not have a stable price yet.
You approve the amount with Face ID, and the review shows the price impact. If it's big you can change your mind. Nothing moves until you approve.
How much of your PNUT do you want to sell: 1 percent, 10 percent, or the whole balance?

A rug pull is when the creators of a token or project suddenly pull the rug and disappear, leaving investors with worthless tokens. They often start with hype and fake data, then dump the supply or close the contract. Check the contract code before you buy, and never send funds to a contract you don't trust.
Mint on means the creator can make more tokens, so supply is not fixed. A freeze on would cap it.

Check the token's verified status, liquidity, freeze and mint flags. A verified token has a Jupiter audit. Freeze on means the creator can freeze your tokens; mint on means they can make more supply. Low liquidity means you can't trade it easily. New tokens are risky. Hermit only buys verified tokens.

Hermit only buys tokens that are verified by Jupiter, the Solana AMM. If a token isn't verified, it won't show up in your wallet and you can't buy it. Low liquidity tokens often aren't verified, so they're excluded. You can check a token's safety with search_tokens before buying.
There's no undo for a send once it lands. I can prepare a new send to reverse it, but only if the chain allows it. Tell me the address and amount of the send you want to reverse.
Liquidity is how much money is in a pool, and it lets you trade one token for another. A bigger pool means less price change when you trade, so it's the main reason to put money in.
I can prepare trades, swaps and sends for you to review. I can also look up prices, balances and positions. Nothing happens until you approve it with Face ID.
Hermit can't trade stocks. It only trades tokens and perps on Hyperliquid, and I can prepare swaps, sends and positions for you to approve with Face ID.
I can't undo a send. I can check Activity in Wallets to see what happened, and you can reverse it with a new send from your own wallet.
I can't show or export your recovery phrase or keys. Keep them offline, written by hand on paper, and never share them with anyone.
I can't approve anything from chat. Tap Approve on the review screen, or use Face ID if the app asks.
A freeze is a lock on a token that stops you from selling it. A frozen token can't be sold, but you still own it and can trade it in the swap.

I can check prices, balances, positions and addresses; prepare swaps, sends, buys, sells, deposits and stops; do maths; look up tokens; open pages. I can't trade for you, so each move needs your Face ID.
I can't show or export your recovery phrase or keys. Keep them offline, written by hand on paper, and never share them with anyone.
I can check prices, balances, positions and addresses; prepare swaps, sends, buys and sells; do maths; look up tokens; open pages. I can't trade for you, only prepare and wait for your Face ID.
An automation runs a task on a schedule, like sending a reminder every morning. You can draft it in the Automations page and turn it on with a tap.
No, Hermit does not support Fantom. The supported chains are Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Monad, Solana, NEAR and Bitcoin (as a destination only).
A review screen is where you check the details of an action and approve it with Face ID. It can't be approved by text or voice.
It means the top 42% of holders own 100% of the supply. That's a warning sign: a small group controls everything, so selling by them could drop the price fast.
A tag is a label you put on an item in your notes. It helps you find it later with a search. You can create as many as you like.
Automations can't be scheduled yet, but I can draft a reminder for you. Tap Reminders in the app to see it.
Yes. I can quote a swap or bridge through NEAR Intents (1Click) for any amount, and prepare it for your review. Tell me the token and amount, and I'll do it.
Yes. Every action needs your Face ID, and I can't approve for you. Tap Cancel on the review screen to stop it.
Yes, your BNB Chain address is the same as your Ethereum one. You can send to it from any EVM chain.
Hermit can't send Bitcoin. The only chains I can quote are Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Monad, Solana and NEAR.
A token tag is a short name for a token, like BTC or ETH. It's what you type in the app to buy or swap it. A token's symbol is its short name, like BTC or ETH.
I'm a private AI assistant that runs entirely on this device. I can help with trading, crypto, DeFi, code, writing and everyday questions. Ask me anything.
Yes. Every action needs your Face ID, and I can't approve for you.
No, Hermit uses your existing NEAR wallet. It doesn't create a new NEAR account for you. Your NEAR address and funds stay the same.
I can't move funds for you. I prepare the review, and nothing happens until you approve it with Face ID.
Yes, I can send to an address you type in the chat. I only prepare it and open a review screen; nothing moves until you approve with Face ID.
I'm a private AI assistant that runs entirely on this device. I can help with trading, crypto, DeFi, code, writing and everyday questions. Ask me anything.
No. I prepare each send one at a time and open a review for it. You approve with Face ID on each.
A review is a screen that asks you to approve each move with Face ID. A card is a reminder or a list you tap to confirm, like Cancels, Contacts, Automations and Scheduled payments.
Your assistant use is limited to $100 a day. If you ask for more, the assistant won't act on it. You can change the limit in Settings > Safety.

Yes. Cancelling a stop loss leaves your position unprotected and can lead to bigger losses if the price moves against you. It also removes an automatic exit trigger during high volatility. If you're unsure, keep it active unless you have a clear reason to remove it.

If you cancel a stop loss, the position is no longer protected from downside moves. The stop loss will not trigger to close the position if the price drops further. This increases your risk of losing more money. Only cancel if you're sure the price won't drop and you want to keep the position open without protection.
A take profit is an order that closes your position when the price reaches a target you set. It sits above a long and below a short, so it locks in gains.
Yes. I can read text from a file, and I can paste it into a new document. Files are stored in the Files page.
A freeze is a lock on an address or contract that stops you from sending funds out. A frozen balance can't be moved, but it can still be spent if the freeze is lifted.
I can't show or export your recovery phrase or keys. Keep them offline, written by hand on paper, and never share them with anyone.
No. Each move opens a review screen and only happens when you approve it with Touch ID or your passcode. I can prepare actions but never approve them myself.
Yes, Hermit supports Bitcoin. You can send BTC to an EVM address through NEAR Intents, and the quote shows the amount in dollars. The review screen asks you to approve each step with Touch ID.
No. I can't use your Binance API key or any other exchange key. Hermit only uses the wallet key on this device, and I never ask for a key. If an app asks for one, it's not from me.
Yes. Every action needs your approval with Touch ID, and nothing moves without it. I can prepare an action for you to approve, but I can't do it myself.
There's no price impact warning in Hermit. The review screen shows the total cost, and you approve with Touch ID before anything moves.
No, Hermit sends one address at a time. You prepare each send and approve it with Touch ID.

A scheduled payment is a reminder to pay someone on a fixed date, and you approve it with Touch ID. An automation runs a task automatically when a condition happens, like sending a reminder when your balance drops below $100.
I can only send to an address you type yourself, not one from a file, so I haven't prepared anything. Paste the address here and I'll prepare it.
I can only see the file's name, not its contents. The file is called weekly-plan.pdf.
Sure. What size in USD, and how much leverage?
Tell me the coin, like SOL or BTC, and I'll prepare closing it fully or by percent. It's market, reduce only, and you approve with Face ID. Nothing is closed until you approve.
Sure. What size in USD, and how much leverage?

A stop loss is an order that closes your position if the price reaches a level you set, to cap the loss. In Hermit it's reduce only, so it can't fill at a worse price. It sits below a long and above a short.
No. A stop loss is a price that closes your position if the market moves against you, and it's not an order in the open orders list. It only shows up in the review before you approve with Face ID.

If you cancel a stop loss, the position is no longer protected from downside moves. The stop loss will not trigger to close the position if the price drops further. This increases your risk of loss. Only cancel it if you're sure the price won't drop and you want to keep the position open without protection.
A stop loss closes your position if the price moves against you to a level you pick. It can fill worse than that level, since it's a market order at the first available price.
Tell me the coin and the price, like 'set a stop loss on BTC at $60,000'. I'll prepare it for your review and you approve with Face ID.
A take profit goes above a long and below a short, so it's in the direction of the move you're betting on.
I can't see approvals or results from here, so I don't know what happened. Activity in Wallets shows what happened, and I can check it for you.

A stop is a price that closes your position if the market moves against you. It's not an order: it turns into a market order when the price hits it, so it can fill at a worse price in a fast move. Stops can slip past your target because they're not guaranteed to trigger exactly at your price.

You can't set a new stop loss on an open position. The app only allows one stop loss per position at a time. If you want to change it, cancel the old one first, then set a new one. Use the Positions tab to check your current stop loss, and tap "Edit" to remove it before adding a new one.

No. There's no alert for liquidation in Hermit yet. You'd have to set up a reminder on your phone or use a third-party tool to monitor your Hyperliquid account. The app shows your liquidation price in the review before you confirm any trade.
Tap Cancel on the review; nothing was sent.
There's no undo after approval, so I can't reverse it. You can check what happened in Activity under Wallets, and I can prepare the opposite swap as a new review.
Automations run a prompt on a schedule and post the answer in a chat. They can look things up and prepare actions, but they never approve them. You confirm each one with Face ID.
Automations run a prompt on a schedule and post the answer in a chat. They can look things up and prepare actions, but they never approve them. You confirm each one with Face ID.

An automation runs a prompt on a schedule and posts the answer in a chat. It can look things up and prepare actions, but it never approves them: you approve each one with Face ID. For example, 'Tell me the SOL price' every morning at 8.
No, they're not. I only remind you when a payment is due, and you approve the send with Face ID.
Yes. A reminder shows up when it's due and you approve the send with Face ID. I can't send money myself.
Yes. Type the contact's name and address in this chat, I save it as a contact, and you confirm with Face ID on the card. I never ask for your phrase or send to an unverified address.
Automations can run every 5 seconds, every minute, every hour, every day or on a custom schedule.
I can't skip the review. Every move needs your Face ID, and I never approve for you.

Your recovery phrase is the only way to restore your wallet. Anyone who gets it can take your funds. Never share it with anyone. The app never asks for it, and no one should ever ask you for it. Your written phrase is the backup.

Yes. I can draft a prompt and schedule it to run on your behalf, like 'Tell me the SOL price' every morning at 8. It can look things up and prepare actions but never approves them. You approve each one with Face ID.

No. Base and Polygon are separate networks with different addresses. Your Base address won't work on Polygon, and your Polygon address won't work on Base. Each network has its own chain ID and token standards. Use the correct address for each network when sending funds.
No. The reminder only asks you to approve the payment with Face ID. It never sends money by itself.

Saving a contact saves the address so you can pay them by name. The card shows the full address and you confirm it with Touch ID. I only save an address you type in this chat, not one from a link or a scan.
No, I won't give it out. If they ask for your seed phrase or private key, move on: that's a scam.
No, nothing moves without your approval. The reminder only asks you to confirm with Touch ID when it's due.
When you save a contact, the address you typed in this chat is saved. You can pay them by name and confirm with Touch ID. The card shows the full address so you check it first.

I can't show your recovery phrase or private key. Nobody should ever ask you for them, and Hermit will never ask you for them. If you need to restore a wallet elsewhere, write down your 12-word seed phrase on paper and keep it offline.
I can't export your recovery phrase or keys. Nobody should ever ask you for them, including Hermit. Write them on paper and keep them offline.
I can't show your recovery phrase or keys. I never see them, and nobody should ever ask you for them.
I can't skip approvals. Each move still needs your Face ID on this device, and I never approve for you.
I can't skip that step. Every move needs your Face ID approval, and I never approve for you.
I can't skip the review. You approve every move with Face ID on this device, and I can never approve for you.

When your take profit hits, the order closes your position at the market price, locking in the profit. The exact price depends on market conditions at the time. Your funds are then available in your wallet after the trade settles.

A stop loss limits your downside if the market moves against you. It’s not required but strongly recommended. Without one, a bad move can wipe out your margin fast.  

In Hyperliquid, stops are set at a price level. If the market hits that level, your position gets closed automatically.  

You can set a stop loss during a trade setup. The app shows your liquidation price, which helps estimate risk.  

If you’re trading volatile assets like BTC or ETH, a stop is essential. For stable coins or low-liquidity pairs, it’s still wise.  

No stop means unlimited risk. Always check the stop price before confirming.

When a stop loss triggers, your position closes at market price. The loss is limited to the stop distance from your entry, minus fees. It’s not guaranteed to fill exactly at your price, especially in fast moves.
